events.title: Claude Fable 5 access restored after US lifts export controls
events.quote: As of today, June 30, the export controls on Fable 5 and Mythos 5 have been lifted. Fable 5 will be available starting tomorrow, Wednesday, July 1, to users globally on the Claude Platform, Claude.ai, Claude Code, and Claude Cowork.
events.note: Resolves the 18-day suspension (paired event id anthropic-fable-mythos-gov-suspension-2026). Timeline: Commerce Dept lifted the export controls on 2026-06-30; Fable 5 returned globally on 2026-07-01 across Claude Platform, Claude.ai, Claude Code, and Claude Cowork. To secure the lift, Anthropic (working with the government) trained an improved safety classifier that blocks the specific jailbreak technique from the Amazon report in over 99% of cases; developers may see a higher false-positive rate on vulnerability-adjacent debugging. Mythos 5 was separately restored earlier to a set of US organizations following government approval on 2026-06-26, with broader domestic/international Glasswing-program access still being coordinated. Corroborated by CNBC, NBC News, Al Jazeera, The Hacker News, 9to5Mac. permanent:true / ends_on null = standing change (access is back for good, no countdown). consumer_impact favorable via kind=restoration (dir +1), offsetting the removal's -1 so Anthropic's drift reads as the round-trip it was.

events.title: Claude Fable 5 & Mythos 5 suspended by US government directive
events.quote: We received the directive from the government today at 5:21pm (ET). ... We apologize for this disruption to our customers. We believe this is a misunderstanding and are working to restore access as soon as possible.
events.note: On 2026-06-12 (~5:21pm ET) the US government issued an export-control directive ordering Anthropic to suspend ALL access to Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5; Anthropic complied the same evening. Per secondary reporting (9to5Mac, Decrypt, TechCrunch) the directive came from the Commerce Department (Secretary Howard Lutnick, drafted with the Bureau of Industry and Security) after a third party (Amazon researchers) demonstrated a jailbreak that got the model to identify software vulnerabilities and write exploit code, raising national-security concerns; it barred access by any foreign national inside or outside the US, including foreign-national Anthropic employees. First time a US lab was forced to pull a generally available model. RESOLVED: the Commerce Department lifted the export controls on 2026-06-30 and Fable 5 returned globally on 2026-07-01 (18-day outage); ends_on set to 2026-06-30 (the last day the suspension was in effect) so this now renders as 'ended' while the paired restoration goes live on 2026-07-01. See the paired restoration event (id anthropic-fable-mythos-restored-2026). SUPERSEDED the earlier Jun 9-22 free-window promo (source https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-fable-5-mythos-5), which was moot while the models were unavailable. This also coincided with a force-reset of subscription weekly limits on the evening of Fri 2026-06-12 (observed, not stated in the directive).

events.title: Claude Code weekly limit +50%
events.quote: Claude Code weekly limits are increasing 50%, now through July 13. Live now for all Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise users.
events.note: Reported verbatim from the official @ClaudeDevs post (May 13, 2026). Temporary lift on the WEEKLY cap only; paid plans (Pro/Max/Team/seat-based Enterprise), not Free or API/usage-based. Expires Jul 13, 6PM PDT unless extended. Stacks on the permanent 5-hour 2x.

events.title: Claude Code 5-hour limit doubled
events.quote: Anthropic announced it was doubling Claude Code five-hour rate limits for Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise plans and removing peak-hours limit reduction for Claude Code on Pro and Max.
events.note: Permanent (no expiry announced). Doubles the rolling 5-hour cap and removed peak-hour throttling for Pro/Max on Claude Code. The temporary weekly +50% (separate event) stacks on top through Jul 13.

events.title: Copilot moves to usage-based billing (AI Credits)
events.quote: Starting June 1, premium request units (PRUs) will be replaced by GitHub AI Credits.
events.note: Billing-model change, not a promo. Premium request units (PRUs) are replaced by GitHub AI Credits, consumed by token usage (input, output, cached) at each model's published API rate. Monthly price is unchanged but now bundles a matching credit pool: Pro $10/mo incl $10 in credits, Pro+ $39/mo incl $39 in credits; Business $19/seat, Enterprise $39/seat. Existing annual Pro/Pro+ subscribers stay on PRU-based pricing until their plan expires (with model multipliers rising Jun 1 for annual plans). GitHub shipped a preview-bill experience in early May so users could project costs before the switch. consumer_impact: unfavorable — on balance a tightening for active users: a fixed monthly request allowance becomes a depletable metered pool you can exhaust mid-cycle, and annual-plan model multipliers rise, even though the sticker price held. No published per-plan number moved, so this is a sourced human judgment (widely reported as a downgrade), not a measured delta — which is why it drives the drift verdict but not the changelog.

events.title: AI Plus cut to $4.99, storage doubled, base AI credits dropped
events.quote: Decrease in price: The standard monthly price of your AI Plus plan will be lowered from $7.99/month to $4.99/month, and annual plans will be lowered from $79.99/year to $49.99/year. Increase in storage: We're doubling the amount of cloud storage included with your AI Plus plan from 200 GB to 400 GB. While 200 AI credits will no longer be included as a benefit in your base plan each month, the new usage limit model we are introducing should allow you to maintain the same experience you are used to.
events.note: Source: official Google email to AI Plus subscribers, June 8, 2026 (corroborated by 9to5Google, Engadget, Android Police). Three concurrent changes: (1) price down $7.99->$4.99/mo and $79.99->$49.99/yr, applied next 1-2 billing cycles or at offer-period end; (2) cloud storage 200GB->400GB, rolling out over a few days; (3) the bundled 200 AI credits/month are removed from the base plan as Google shifts to product-based, compute-weighted usage limits (factoring prompt complexity, features used, chat length; 5h refresh + weekly cap; AI Plus still 2x non-subscriber). The AI-credit usage model is rolling out to other products starting with Flow and Antigravity. Per Google One support, AI credits remain purchasable only on AI Pro/Ultra, not AI Plus. Public pricing pages (one.google.com, gemini.google) still showed old $7.99/200GB at time of capture; snapshot row stays as-is (never edit a past snapshot) until the next snapshot confirms the new figures.

events.title: Claude Cowork 5-hour limit doubled (promo)
events.quote: Anthropic doubled Claude Cowork's five-hour session rate limits for Pro, Max, and Team subscribers from 5 June through 5 July 2026, leaving weekly caps and the shared quota across Claude products unchanged.
events.note: Announced by Boris Cherny (leads Claude Code at Anthropic) via social post on 2026-06-05; free, no opt-in, no billing change. Cowork-SURFACE only: doubles the rolling 5-hour session cap in Claude Cowork; the weekly cap and the shared quota across Claude products are unchanged, and Claude Code / Claude.ai keep their standard session limits. Applies to Pro, Max, Team and legacy seat-based Enterprise; excludes Free and consumption-based Enterprise seats. Auto-expires 2026-07-05, after which Cowork 5-hour limits revert with no action needed. Distinct from the permanent Claude Code 5h 2x (id anthropic-claudecode-5h-2x-2026) and the Claude Code weekly +50% (id anthropic-claudecode-weekly-plus50-2026) - different surface. Confidence 'announced' (exec social post, corroborated by The New Stack, KuCoin; no stable Anthropic doc page).

events.title: Cursor Teams adds Premium seat, splits usage into two pools
events.quote: These changes will start for all new customers immediately, and renewing customers on billing cycles starting July 1st, 2026.
events.note: Official Cursor blog. Three Teams-plan changes effective 2026-07-01 (new customers immediately; renewing customers on cycles starting Jul 1): (1) a new Premium seat at $96/seat/mo annual ($120/seat/mo monthly) giving 5x the included usage of a Standard seat, aimed at the heaviest agent users; (2) each Teams seat now carries TWO separate included-usage pools - Composer + Auto (reserved for first-party Cursor models) and Third-Party API (third-party models) - instead of one shared dollar pool; (3) dashboard shows proximity to each pool's limit and admins can set dollar-threshold smart alerts via Slack/email. Cursor states the changes 'will lower costs for 90% of teams,' and that Premium's Composer pool covers a full month of heavy agent usage for 99% of users. consumer_impact left null (neutral context): it is a structural re-slice with a company-claimed net saving for most but a new higher-priced power tier and pool-splitting, no single published number moving in a scoreable direction - so it appears as context, not a scored drift signal. The individual Cursor plans (Pro $20, Pro+ $60, Ultra $200) are unchanged and were re-verified 2026-07-01.

events.title: Anthropic pauses the Agent SDK separate-credit billing change
events.quote: "Nothing changes for now," the company told by email.
events.note: Reverses the change captured in the 2026-06-08 snapshot as three announced Agent SDK surface rows (effective_on 2026-06-15). On the day it was due (2026-06-15) Anthropic paused it: Agent SDK, `claude -p`, Claude Code GitHub Actions, and third-party apps authing via the Agent SDK CONTINUE to draw from the existing Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise subscription pools rather than a separate metered dollar credit. No new credit to claim; nothing changed for subscribers. Because the separate-credit surface never took effect, the 2026-07-01 snapshot drops those three Agent SDK rows (they show as 'removed' in the changelog vs 2026-06-08). Widely reported (The New Stack, The Decoder, DevOps.com) as a consumer-favorable reversal, likely tied to OpenAI's looming API price cuts and Anthropic's IPO timing. consumer_impact favorable: keeping SDK usage inside the subscription pool is a de-facto win for developers vs the announced metered credit. permanent:false because Anthropic framed it as a pause ('for now'), not a cancellation - revisit if they re-announce.

resets.detail: Rolling 5-hour session window. The 5-hour timer starts when you first reach the cap, and your allowance resets 5 hours after that — not on a fixed daily clock. Settings > Usage shows time remaining in the current session.

Weekly cap (applies across all models) resets at a fixed time each week that is assigned to your account — so the reset day/time varies per account, with no single global moment. Runs alongside the 5-hour session limit.
Rolling 3-hour window. ChatGPT shows the reset time when you hit the cap; until it resets, chats fall back to a mini version of the model rather than blocking.
Thinking-model messages also carry a weekly allowance that refreshes on a rolling 7-day basis; the in-product reset time is shown when you reach it.
Under Google's product-based usage-limit model (Gemini), allowances refresh on a 5-hour basis on top of a weekly cap, weighted by prompt complexity and features used rather than a flat message count.
A weekly cap sits above the 5-hour refresh in Gemini's usage-limit model; subscribers get a higher multiple of the free-tier allowance.

Base 200 AI credits/mo were removed; Google uses a compute-based 5h + weekly usage model, AI Plus still 2x non-subscriber. No price-value change vs the 2026-06-08 snapshot (already recorded 4.99), so no changelog delta.

entries.quote: Get 4x higher usage limits than Free
entries.notes: Google moved from daily prompt counts to opaque compute-based limits (5h refresh + weekly cap), then adjusted them after May 2026 backlash. No published numeric cap. Price $19.99/mo and 4x-vs-Free multiplier re-verified on gemini.google/subscriptions 2026-07-01. Ultra multipliers are stated relative to Pro.

entries.quote: $99.99/month: 5x higher usage limits vs. AI Pro
entries.notes: Multiplier is official; absolute compute budget is not published. Lower of the two AI Ultra price points. Re-verified on gemini.google/subscriptions 2026-07-01.

entries.quote: $199.99/month: 20x higher usage limits vs. AI Pro
entries.notes: Price dropped from $250 to $199.99 in May 2026. Multiplier official; absolute budget not published. Re-verified on gemini.google/subscriptions 2026-07-01.

entries.quote: SuperGrok offers 1,000 messages and 50 images per day; on the standard plan you can send approximately 100 to 150 messages per four-hour window before being throttled.
entries.notes: 4h figure is a community midpoint of the 100-150 range. $30/mo or $300/yr. Not re-verified for 2026-07-01: xAI's own limits page (x.ai) is Cloudflare-gated (no_feed), and on re-check 2026-07-01 the cited community source (jingrey) had been rewritten to a per-feature format (images/video/voice/DeepSearch caps) that no longer states the 1,000/day message total, and it now lists SuperGrok Heavy at $80/mo. That single, internally-inconsistent secondary source is not enough to overwrite these figures, so the 2026-06-07 values and verified_on are carried forward unchanged pending a dedicated community/official re-verification. confidence stays community.

entries.quote: SuperGrok Heavy lifts the caps to 5,000 messages and 200 images daily; Heavy subscribers see roughly 250 messages per four-hour window.
entries.notes: Only consumer plan with full Grok 4.3 access. $300/mo. Not re-verified for 2026-07-01 (see SuperGrok note): the cited community source now shows a conflicting $80/mo Heavy price and a different per-feature cap structure with no daily message total, uncorroborated by any other source, so the 2026-06-07 figures and verified_on are carried forward pending dedicated re-verification. If a Heavy price cut is confirmed it would be a material change - flagged for follow-up.

entries.quote: Perplexity Pro includes approximately 500 Deep Research queries per day at average usage.
entries.notes: Pro users reported quiet limit cuts to advanced models in May 2026. Chat 'unlimited' applies to the UI, not API. Not re-verified for 2026-07-01: Perplexity's blog/hub is a JS-rendered site with no scrapeable source (no_feed), and secondary sources checked 2026-07-01 now cite a much lower Pro Deep Research allowance (~20/day) that conflicts with this 500/day figure. The sources disagree and none is authoritative, so the 2026-06-07 value and verified_on are carried forward pending a dedicated re-verification against Perplexity's own page. confidence stays community.

entries.quote: Perplexity Max includes the highest available limits across all features, plus 10,000 Perplexity Computer credits per month.
entries.notes: Exact daily query cap for Max is not published. $200/mo or $2,000/yr. Not re-verified live for 2026-07-01 (see Pro note); value is null/unpublished either way, so carried forward unchanged.

entries.quote: $20 of API agent usage
entries.notes: Two separate monthly pools: API agent usage (the $ figure) plus a non-numeric 'generous Auto and Composer usage' pool. On-demand usage billed in arrears after the included amount. Re-verified on cursor.com/pricing 2026-07-01 ($20/mo, $20 included API usage). The 2026-07-01 Cursor Teams pricing change (new Premium seat, split pools; event cursor-teams-pricing-premium-seat-2026) applies to Teams/Business seats, not this individual Pro plan, which is unchanged.

measured.notes: Realized consumption for one billing month, not a cap. The API pool ran ~$33 against a stated 'at least $20' floor: gpt-5.5-medium used 42.8% of the pool for 30M tokens; at the Pro+-validated rate of ~$0.47/M that is ~$13.9, implying a ~$33 pool. Other API-pool models aren't individually itemized on the Pro screenshot, so only the observed gpt-5.5-medium rate is listed; see Pro+ for the full per-model rate card (rates are model-intrinsic API prices, shared across plans). Auto+Composer hit 100% and overflowed 16.9M tokens into the API pool. ~95% of all tokens are subsidized Auto.

entries.quote: $70 of API agent usage
entries.notes: Plus a non-numeric 'generous Auto and Composer usage' pool. On-demand usage billed in arrears after the included amount. Re-verified on cursor.com/pricing 2026-07-01 ($60/mo, $70 included API usage). Individual plan unaffected by the 2026-07-01 Cursor Teams pricing change.

measured.source: Cursor dashboard, account-owner screenshot + usage CSV export
measured.notes: Updated replacement for the earlier Pro+ receipt, not a separate report. Cursor dashboard showed the Pro+ billing period May 10-Jun 08 fully maxed: Total spend $512.83, Included $512.83, On-demand $0, and the included pools at 100% Auto and 100% API used. The CSV export for the period contains 914.2M included tokens: 137.4M API-model tokens (claude-opus-4-8-thinking-high + gpt-5.5-medium) and 776.8M Auto/Composer tokens. The CSV also contains 21.3M Free tokens and 1.7M errored/no-charge tokens; those are excluded from the included monthly receipt. Per-model $/M rates are not listed here because this CSV labels rows as Included/Free rather than giving precise per-model dollar charges.

entries.quote: $400 of API agent usage

Re-verified on cursor.com/pricing 2026-07-01 ($200/mo, $400 included API usage). Individual plan unaffected by the 2026-07-01 Cursor Teams pricing change.

Unlimited code completions. $10/mo and 300/mo re-verified on docs.github.com 2026-07-01 (additional premium requests $0.04 each).

entries.notes: Per seat. Larger monthly pool of AI credits plus priority access to new models; per-seat credit amount not published per-plan. $39/seat/mo re-verified on docs.github.com 2026-07-01.
